messages.author: e3cd7ac95409208e
messages.subject: Polychoric correlations in mirt. Possible?
parts:
Hi Phil. Just me with another small question here.

I find myself having to deal with both ordinal AND missing data. I remember in our brief exchange that you clarified the estimators used in mirt all of 'full information' type and, therefore, suitable for missing data (without needing to explicitly invoke FIML as it is done in lavaan or Mplus).

Now, lavaan has a function called lavCor() where one can obtain polychoric correlations by fitting an unrestricted model to the data. I am wondering if mirt has a similar function or is there any way to trick the syntax into giving a full polychoric correlation matrix so that I wouldn't have to resort to multiple imputation to obtain my parameter estimates.

I don't think full-information estimators rely on the intermediate step of  calculating a  polychoric correlation matrix but I thought it didn't hurt to ask. 

Thank you!

- Elia

On Thu, Mar 23, 2017 at 12:26 AM, Sabeeh Baig <sabeeh...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Elia,

I'm burning the midnight candle as well and thought I'd respond. Which parameter estimates do you think you'd need to use multiple imputation to obtain?

Not parameters, data. It's difficult to deal with missing responses in computing polychoric correlations because the bi-variate tables become unbalanced and potentially sparse; one either has to remove data row-wise, or try at imputation to help diminish the problem. Neither solution is optimal/fool-proof though. Cheers.

Phil

Sabeeh

messages.subject: Re: Polychoric correlations in mirt. Possible?
parts:
Just wanting to open this thread once again to keep it all in one place for ease of reference. 

Leaving the issue of missing data aside, is there a way to obtain polychoric correlations from mirt? Perhaps some sort of 'trick' like fitting a saturated model of some sort? Upon reading the package documentation it mentions:

If the model is an exploratory item factor analysis estimation will begin by computing a matrix of quasi-polychoric correlations.

Is it possible to have access to this matrix of "quasi-polychoric correlations"? (And why the "quasi", btw?)

Thank you!
